reason: The fusion proteins match adjacent myoblast membranes, suggesting they can join the precursors into a multinucleated fibre.
expectation: The myoblasts will fuse into a multinucleated muscle cell.

effect: The fused fibre has sliding filaments but its actin grip sites remain covered; the calcium signal is the likely next step.
reaction: The distinction between one fibre and its many nuclei is useful.
reason: The calcium pulse spreads around the fibre's filaments and should trigger its pulling machinery.
expectation: Calcium will expose actin's grip sites and allow the fibre to pull.

effect: Calcium exposed the grip sites and the fibre shortened through filament sliding; it now needs calcium removed to become ready again.
reaction: The distinction between filament sliding and filament shortening is useful.
reason: The calcium-pumping membranes should return calcium to storage so the fibre can reset.
expectation: Calcium will be pumped back into storage and the fibre will relax, ready for another signal.

effect: Calcium pumping stopped pulling and left the fibre ready to respond again, completing the first goal.
reaction: It is useful to see that relaxation also requires ATP and an outside pull to lengthen the fibre.
reason: The empty biceps sheaths provide spaces for muscle fibres and connect them to tendons.
expectation: The fibres will fill the biceps sheaths to form a muscle with tendons.

effect: The fibre first needed connective layers to form fascicles; there are enough bundles for both muscles.
reaction: The distinction between a fibre's membrane and its surrounding connective layer is helpful, though I had missed that intermediate step.
reason: The fascicles can now fill the biceps sheaths and connect to their tendons.
expectation: The fascicles will form the biceps within its tendon-connected sheaths.

effect: The fascicles formed the biceps, with connective tissue carrying force toward its tendons. The triceps still needs to be built.
reaction: The force pathway from fibres to tendon is useful.
reason: The remaining fascicles should fill the triceps sheaths just as they filled the biceps sheaths.
expectation: The fascicles will form the triceps within its tendon-connected sheaths.

effect: The triceps is built with three heads and a shared tendon; both muscles now need attachment to the skeleton.
reaction: The different paths of the triceps heads clarify their anatomy.
reason: The biceps tendons lead toward the shoulder and radius, so the movable arm skeleton is the natural attachment site.
expectation: The biceps tendons will attach to the arm skeleton across the elbow.
